title: EG CP 5 cowpea (EG cowpea 5): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: EG CP 5 cowpea: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: EG CP 5 cowpea is a cowpea variety. 48 to 50 days to harvest, 7 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: EG CP 5 is a registered cowpea variety, also sold or known as EG cowpea 5. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Cp 05. BPI NCRDC Los Baños, Laguna bred it. It takes 48 to 50 days from sowing to the first harvest, with 7 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for EG cowpea 5, this is the same cowpea. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [cowpea variety finder](/crop-varieties/cowpea), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

EG CP 5 cowpea takes 48 to 50 days from sowing to the first harvest. That is 4.3 days faster than the average of the 13 cowpea varieties with a day count, 53.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 7 t/ha beats the average of its group, 5.44. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives first harvest 48 to 50 days, last harvest 74 to 76 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: The pests and diseases that hit cowpea fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its pods grew about 21.83 cm long. A hundred seeds weigh about 16.77 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is maroon.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** About 7 t/ha in both seasons in registration trials.
**Fruit:** Green pods about 17 to 22 cm, maroon seeds, about 15 to 17 g per 100 seeds.
Highly tolerant to fusarium wilt, rust and mosaic virus.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: bPI cowpea in the NSIC registry, listed for both wet and dry seasons, current seed sellers not confirmed. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant EG CP 5 cowpea

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Cowpea fits the dry season after rice, on the moisture the paddy keeps. Pick by use: green pods for vegetables, or dry seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is EG cowpea 5 the same as EG CP 5?
items.a: Yes. EG cowpea 5 is another name for EG CP 5, registered as NSIC 1995 Cp 05. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 48 to 50 days from sowing to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 7 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of EG CP 5?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
